title: Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga: Temple Guide near Ellora
seoTitle: Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga near Ellora: Temple Guide | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: Visit Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga at Verul beside the Ellora Caves: the temple, darshan customs, how to reach from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and nearby sights.
description: A visitor's guide to Grishneshwar (Ghrishneshwar) Jyotirlinga at Verul: the legend of Ghushma, the red-stone temple restored by Ahilyabai Holkar, darshan customs, how to reach from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, combining it with the Ellora Caves, Daulatabad and Shirdi, and the best time.
dek: The last of the twelve Jyotirlingas in the traditional list stands a short walk from the Ellora Caves, so one day covers both.

hero.alt: The red-stone Grishneshwar Temple at Verul, near Ellora, Maharashtra

intro: Grishneshwar Temple, also spelt Ghrishneshwar or Grushneshwar, is in Verul village, about 1.5 km from the Ellora Caves and about 30 km from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (formerly Aurangabad). Tradition links it to Ghushma, a devotee whose faith was rewarded by Shiva, which gives the temple its name.

The present temple of red basalt was restored in the 18th century by Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore, who also rebuilt many other temples across India; an earlier restoration is credited to Maloji Bhosale, grandfather of Shivaji. It is one of the smaller Jyotirlinga temples, and queues are usually shorter than at the more famous shrines.
quickAnswer: Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga is at Verul, about 1.5 km from the Ellora Caves and about 30 km from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. Most visitors combine darshan with Ellora in one day; note that Ellora is closed on Tuesdays. Men are usually asked to remove shirts before entering the sanctum. October to March is the best time, and Mondays and Shivratri are the busiest days.
takeaways: Grishneshwar is 1.5 km from the Ellora Caves and about 30 km from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.
The red-stone temple was restored by Ahilyabai Holkar in the 18th century.
Men are usually asked to remove shirts before entering the sanctum.
Combine it with Ellora (closed on Tuesdays), Daulatabad and Shirdi.
Queues are usually shorter than at the bigger Jyotirlingas, except on Mondays and festivals.

sections.heading: The temple
paras: The temple has a five-tiered shikhara and a hall of carved red stone, with sculptures of deities and scenes from the epics. Devotees can often touch the linga in the sanctum, which is unusual among the Jyotirlingas; follow the priests' instructions and the rules posted at the entrance.

sections.heading: Darshan customs
list: Men are usually asked to remove shirts and vests before entering the sanctum.
Leather belts and bags may not be allowed inside.
Weekday mornings are quietest; Mondays, Shravan and Maha Shivratri are busiest.
Photography inside the sanctum is not allowed.

items.name: Ellora Caves
body: A UNESCO World Heritage Site of Buddhist, Hindu and Jain cave temples, including the monolithic Kailasa temple (Cave 16). Closed on Tuesdays.

items.name: Daulatabad Fort
body: A hilltop fortress about 15 km away on the road to the city.

items.name: Shirdi
body: The Sai Baba temple town, about 100 km away, often combined on the same trip.

body: Bibi Ka Maqbara and the city's gates and markets.

sections.heading: How to reach and where to stay
list: From Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar: about 30 km by taxi or bus, around 45 minutes.
The city has an airport and a railway station with connections to Mumbai, Pune, Delhi and Hyderabad.
From Shirdi: about 100 km; from Nashik: about 185 km.
Stay in the city for more choice, or at simple lodges in Verul near the temple and caves.

sections.heading: The legend of Ghushma
paras: According to the Shiva Purana, Ghushma was a devout woman who made and worshipped clay lingas every day and immersed them in a nearby tank. When her son was killed out of jealousy, she continued her worship calmly, and Shiva restored the boy and remained here as Ghushmeshwar at her request. The story is told to pilgrims as a lesson in faith and forgiveness, and the tank near the temple is associated with it.

safety: Darshan waits vary from minutes to many hours; no one can guarantee quick darshan, so plan buffer time.
Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered) and follow the temple's rules on phones, bags and photography.
Carry water and a hat for Ellora, which is exposed to the sun.
packing: Modest clothing that is easy to adjust for the sanctum
Slip-on footwear and socks for hot stone floors
Hat, sunscreen and water for Ellora
Cash for offerings, parking and snacks

faqs.q: How far is Grishneshwar from Ellora?
faqs.a: About 1.5 km; you can walk or take a short auto ride.

faqs.q: Do men have to remove shirts at Grishneshwar?
faqs.a: Men are usually asked to remove shirts and vests before entering the sanctum.

faqs.q: How far is Grishneshwar from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad)?
faqs.a: About 30 km, around 45 minutes by road.

faqs.q: Can I visit Grishneshwar and Ellora on the same day?
faqs.a: Yes. Most visitors do both in one day; Ellora is closed on Tuesdays.

faqs.q: What else is there to see near Grishneshwar?
faqs.a: The Ellora Caves, Daulatabad Fort, Khuldabad and Bibi Ka Maqbara in the city; Shirdi is about 100 km away.
Photography inside the sanctum is not allowed; follow the notices at the entrance.
The present temple was restored in the 18th century by Ahilyabai Holkar, after an earlier restoration credited to Maloji Bhosale.
